sources.name: RTB — Setting and reviewing private rents from 1 March 2026

verified_rules.national_rent_control: From 1 March 2026, RTB guidance states that rent in applicable private tenancies may generally be increased once per year by 2% or CPI, whichever is lower, subject to exceptions.
verified_rules.market_reset: For private tenancies created from 1 March 2026, market-rent resetting is permitted in specified circumstances, including at the beginning of a new tenancy in specified circumstances and at the end of a six-year Tenancy of Minimum Duration.
verified_rules.existing_tenancies: For private tenancies created before 1 March 2026, RTB guidance states that market-rent resetting is not available for an ongoing tenancy.
verified_rules.new_apartment_exception: For qualifying new apartments where construction commenced on or after 10 June 2025, RTB guidance states that the 2% cap does not apply and the annual increase is linked to CPI, subject to the applicable conditions.
verified_rules.notice_procedure: RTB guidance states that a rent review notice and copy to the RTB must be served within the specified current procedure; the guidance states that failure to serve the RTB copy makes the notice invalid.

commencement_note: The Irish Statute Book records staged commencement of the 2026 Act, including provisions commencing on 28 February 2026, 1 March 2026 and 3 March 2026; sections 31(1)(a) and 31(1)(b) were listed as not yet commenced on the current consolidated page.
scope_limit: This record is not a complete provision-level treatment of Irish residential tenancy law and must not be used to determine an individual case without full fact and exception analysis.
